done_when: Close no longer runs the full test command on the laptop when the pull request's CI runs it: it runs fast_test when set, otherwise only the test files the change touched and the tests named after its changed source files; CI still runs the full suite and a red CI sends the item back. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body: A newly initialized Node client still runs its full test command locally after it adds an app. Raise: Not done — `src/forge/init.py:61,141` gives new Node repos `[ ! -f package.json ] || (npm ci && npm test)` with no `fast_test`. The `||` matches this fallback guard, so Close runs the entire command instead of selecting related Vitest or Jest tests. This shipped init command is new evidence beyond the earlier ruling about compound npm scripts.
findings.title: Not done: Close no longer runs the full test command on the laptop when the pull request's CI runs it: it runs fast_test when set, otherwise

findings.body: The test named for new and previously adopted clients does not test local selection in either client. Raise: Test — `test_2_new_and_previously_adopted_clients_receive_local_selection_and_full_ci` checks delivered guides and the workflow, but never changes a test or source file and runs `forge close` in those clients. It passes while the shipped Node init command still runs the full suite locally, so it does not prove the Done-when behavior for init or upgrade plus sync.
findings.title: Not done: init and upgrade plus sync local-selection test

stop.reason: Owner chose narrow: pick tests only for Python, Vitest and Jest with each tool's own changed-files option; every other repo runs its full test command as today

why: Each round runs the same tests twice, on the laptop and in CI, which is most of a round's time
